title: Chat compatibility: request framing + function-call idempotency mapper
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce a compatibility adapter that maps Redwood's chat/generation streaming and structured-output semantics to the OpenAI Chat Completions API shape and back. This ticket focuses on two hard problems that have caused recent integration issues: (1) framing of streamed events so legacy OpenAI-compatible clients receive a coherent incremental delta without exposing internal tokenization or Redwood-specific control frames; and (2) deterministic handling and idempotency of function/tool calling semantics when routing requests through fallbacks, retries, or multi-region hedging.
background: We currently support OpenAI-style chat compatibility via several existing shims, but customers report edge cases where streamed fragments re-order, duplicate function call signals are emitted on retries, and structured outputs lose schema markers during chunked streaming. Past tickets implemented naive mappings which solved basic parity but introduced flakiness for SDKs that expect exact OpenAI event ordering and single function_call emission. This causes customer regressions for integrations that perform immediate tool invocation on first function_call event.
proposed_solution: Design a mapping layer that: 1) emits a canonical OpenAI-like SSE event stream that hides Redwood control frames and coalesces multiple internal chunks into stable, ordered delta events; 2) attaches a request fingerprint and idempotency token to each request mapping so retries and hedges can be correlated; 3) converts Redwood structured-output / typed metadata into the OpenAI "function_call" and "content" fields without losing schema paths; 4) exposes an opt-in 'compatibility strict' mode to preserve previous behavior for customers who rely on exact legacy quirks.
decision: Adopt coalescing window approach (50ms or 3 token boundary, whichever comes first) for stream emission to balance latency vs stability. Use a deterministic request fingerprint derived from user request body + model + route that is stable across retries; pair it with a short-lived idempotency token stored in memcache for 60s to dedupe function_call emissions. Implement compatibility strict toggle via request header 'X-Redwood-Compat-Mode: strict|lenient'.
tasks: Spec: write protocol mapping doc describing event types, coalescing rules, idempotency semantics (Confluence: /display/INF/Chat+Compat+Framing)
Runtime: implement stream coalescer component in serving runtime (golang) with pluggable emit policies
API Gateway: inject request fingerprint + idempotency token and propagate as metadata to runtime
Function-call controller: ensure a single authoritative emit and dedupe across retries/hedges
Integration tests: add e2e tests simulating network splits, retries, and hedging across regions
SDK updates: Node & Python SDKs to honor 'compatibility strict' header and handle coalesced deltas
Docs: update OpenAI compatibility guide and migration notes
Canary rollout: enable for 2% of traffic behind feature flag and monitor errors/latency
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral tests show streamed SSE sequence matches OpenAI ordering for 99.99% of trials under simulated packet loss
No duplicated function_call events observed in integration test runs covering retries/hedging
End-to-end latency increase under default coalescing config <= 20ms P50 compared to current baseline
SDK functional tests (Node/Python) pass for both strict and lenient compat modes
Canary rollout metrics: error rate not increased, function-call success rate >= baseline, and customer support regressions < 1% of canary cohort
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Coalescing may increase tail latency for ultra-low-latency customers. Mitigation: provide tunable window header and opt-out via 'compatibility strict' header.
Risk: Idempotency table could grow with retry storms. Mitigation: short TTL (60s) and LRU eviction; add metrics and autoscale memcache if needed.
Risk: Some legacy clients depend on previous non-deduped behavior. Mitigation: 'strict' mode preserves historical behavior and we will document migration steps.
notes: Design review scheduled with API and SDK teams on 2025-02-14; feedback: prefer deterministic fingerprinting over random token for reproducible replay mapping
